## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Lohakumbhijātaka* (Ja 314) is a canonical Jātaka tale translated as *The Copper Pots of Hell* [SuttaCentral]. According to its commentary, the Buddha delivers the story while residing at Jetavana concerning King Pasenadi of Kosala [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. Tormented by an illicit passion for a married woman whose husband he plotted to eliminate, the sleepless king hears four eerie, fragmented sounds in the night—*du*, *sa*, *na*, *so* [Rhys Davids 1917; Bhikkhu Bodhi 2003; Fausböll 1883]. Alarmed, he seeks counsel from his brahmin advisers, who recommend a massive animal sacrifice to avert impending death [Bhikkhu Bodhi 2003; Cowell 1897]. After consulting the Buddha, the king is reassured that the noises pose him no harm: they are the cries of former adulterers taking sixty thousand years to sink and rise in the boiling cauldron of the Lohakumbhī hell, attempting in vain to finish reciting verses of repentance [Bhikkhu Bodhi 2003; Juan Wu 2012; Fausböll 1883]. In the past story (*atītavatthu*), a parallel crisis occurred during the reign of King Brahmadatta of Benares, where the Bodhisatta intervened out of compassion to prevent a slaughter of sacrificial victims [Rhys Davids 1917; UNDV 2009; Juan Wu 2012].

The text was later drawn upon in post-canonical literature, including the northern Thai apocryphal *Māleyyatherasutta* [Cousins et al. 1974]. SuttaCentral notes connections with the *Seṭṭhiputtapetavatthu* (Pv 50) and *Nettippakaraṇa* 37 [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus reports extensive Pali-internal text reuse matching the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, *Saṃyutta-nikāya Sagāthāvagga-aṭṭhakathā*, and the verses of Pv 50, where SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus agree [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records machine-generated cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Jātakamālāṭīkā* (D4151) [DharmaNexus].
